title: SPA/212/2015 of Hazaara Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 212 of 2015
Hazaara Singh ......Appellant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .... Respondents
Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent
nos.1 & 2.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Advocate for the respondent no.3.
Dated : 3rd June, 2015
Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

Writ petitioner is the appellant. The appellant/writ
petitioner filed the writ petition seeking four prayers as follows:
"1. To summon the complete record pertaining to the
case.
2. To issue the Writ, Order or Direction in the nature
of Certiorari quashing the impugned bye-laws nos.18
& 19 of Tehbazari, Bazar Nakhaza Bye-Laws
published in Uttaranchal Gazette on 24.12.2005.
3. To issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of
Mandamus directing the respondents not to interfere in
peaceful holding of the market over the land of the
petitioner situated in Khasra No.94, Village Itawwa,
Tehsil Bajpur, District Udham Singh Nagar.
4. To issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of
Mandamus directing and commanding the respondents
to pay such sum to the petitioner as compensation as
this Hon'ble Court may quantify in the facts and
circumstances of the present case."
2. The appellant is the resident of Village Itawwa, Tehsil
Bajpur, District Udham Singh Nagar. According to him, briefly
put, his case is as follows:
 On account of certain problems, which he raised, the
appellant decided to hold weekly market in his own land. He made
a joint application to Zila Panchayat, Udham Singh Nagar vide
Annexure No.1 to give him permission. The respondent no.3 asked
the appellant to enter into an agreement and to deposit `10,000/- as

2
permission fee. He deposited `10,000/-, being ignorant of the fact
as to whether byelaws were framed and also entered into agreement
as sought to be evidenced by Annexure Nos.2 & 3. The licence was
illegally suspended by the respondent no.3 on 25.09.2014, which
occasioned filing of Writ Petition (M/S) No.2383 of 2014. The
suspension order was quashed by this Court and it was left open to
the respondent authorities to proceed against the appellant in
accordance with law. The appellant continued to hold market. He
made inquiries and he came to know that respondent no.3, which is
Zila Panchayat, Udham Singh Nagar, has framed the impugned
byelaws. Therefore, he has sought relief, which is substantially for
quashing of the impugned byelaws. The learned Single Judge
dismissed the writ petition. Feeling aggrieved, the appellant is
before us.
3. We heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the
learned counsel for Zila Panchayat Shri N.S. Pundir.
4. The byelaws in question are Byelaw Nos. 18 & 19. At the
very first place, we notice that the appellant must fail in regard to
the challenge to the byelaws on the basis that the appellant has
actually sought to quash the byelaws being subordinate legislation.
The appellant cannot be granted relief of quashing the byelaws.
The appellant, if at all, could have sought the relief; it could have
been the relief of declaration. On that ground itself, the appellant
deserves to be non-suited. Even proceeding to examine, however,
the case on merits, we find that there is no merit as found by the
learned Single Judge having regard to the use of the word
'regulation' in Section 239 'D' of The Uttar Pradesh Kshettra
Panchayat and Zila Panchayat Adhiniyam, 1961 (hereinafter
referred to as the Act). Section 239, inter alia, provides as follows:
 Sub Section (1) clearly provides for power to make byelaws
and this Sub-Section is very widely worded.

3
 Sub-Section (2) in fact deals with usual clause in the Statute,
which provides for the particular situation, in which the power can
be exercised. Sub-Section (2) reads as follows:
 "(2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of
the power conferred by sub-section (1), a Zila Panchayat may, in
the exercise of the said power, make any bye-laws described in the
list below: ........."
5. The power under Sub-Section (2) is without prejudice
to the generality of the power under sub-section (1). Therefore,
even if the matter does not fall under sub-section (2), it would
certainly come under the provisions of sub-section (1), provided it
is otherwise covered by sub-section (1). Referring to sub-section
(1), it provides that the Zila Panchayat can make byelaws for its
own purpose and also for the purpose of Kshettra Panchayat. It
must be consistent with the Act and with any Rule. It must be for
promoting and maintaining health, safety and convenience of the
inhabitants of the rural area of the District and for the furtherance
of administration of the Act in the Khand and the District.
Therefore, the key words are 'maintaining health, safety and
convenience of the inhabitants'. As long as the power is exercised
with reference to these broad concepts, there is indeed power de
hors the specific power given in sub-section (2). Coming to
Section 239, it reads as follows:
"239. Power of Zila Panchayat to make bye-laws.-
(1) A Zila Panchayat may, and where required by the
State Government shall, make bye-laws for its own
purposes and for the purposes of Kshettra Panchayats,
applicable to the whole or any part of the rural area of
the district, consistent with this Act and with any rule,
in respect of matters required by this Act to be
governed by bye-laws and for the purposes of
promoting or maintaining the health, safety and
convenience of the inhabitants of the rural area of the
district and for the furtherance of the administration of
this Act in the Khand and the district.

4
(2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality
of the power conferred by sub-section (1), a Zila
Panchayat may, in the exercise of the said power,
make any bye-laws described in the list below:
 A-Building
(a) Declaring with reference to clause (d) of sub-section (2) of Section 164 and alteration of any
specific description to be a "material alteration";
(b) prescribing that, on payment of fees in accordance
with such scale as is specified in this behalf, plans and
specifications shall be obtainable from the Kshettra
Panchayat;
(c) fixing with reference to Section 166 the period for
which a sanction shall remain inforce;
(d) prescribing the type and description of building
which may or may not and the purpose for which a
building may or may not be erected in any prescribed
area or areas within a controlled rural area;
(e) prescribing the circumstances in which a temple
mosque, church or other sacred building may or may
not be erected, re-erected or altered in a controlled
rural area;
(f) prescribing with reference to the erection, re-erection or alteration of buildings, or any class of
buildings, all or any of the following matters-
 (i) the materials and method of construction to
 be used for external and party walls, roofs and
 floor;
 (ii) the position and the materials to be used in
and method of construction of fire-places,
chimneys, drains, latrines, privies, urinals and
cesspools;
 (iii) the height and slope of the roof above the
upper-most floor upon which human beings are
to live or cooking operations are to be carried
on;
 (iv) the ventilation and space to be left about the
building to secure free circulation of air and to
facilitate scavenging and for prevention of fire;
 (v) the level and width of foundation, level of
lowest floor and stability of structure;
 (vi) the number and height of storeys of which
the building may consist;
 (vii) the means to be provided for egress from
the building in case of fire;
 (viii) any other matter affecting the ventilation
or sanitation of building; and
 (ix) the conditions subject to which sanction for
the construction or alteration of a well may be

5
refused or granted, with a view to prevent
pollution of water or danger to any person using
the well;
 (g) regulating, in any manner not specifically provided
for in this Act, the erection of any enclosure, wall,
fence, tent, awning, or other structure, of whatsoever
kind or nature, on any land within a controlled rural
area.
 B-Drains, privies, cesspools, etc.
 (a) Regulating in any manner not specifically provided
for in this Act, the construction, alteration,
maintenance, reservation, cleansing and repair of
drains, ventilation shafts and pipes, water closets,
privies, latrines, urinals, cesspools and other drainage
works;
 (b) regulating or prohibiting the discharge into drains,
or deposit therein, of sewage, sullage, polluted water
and other offensive or obstructive matter.

C-Streets
(a) Determining the information and plans to be
furnished to the Kshettra Panchayat under Section 176;
(b) permitting, prohibiting or regulating the use or
occupation of any or all public streets or places by
itinerant vendors or by any person for the sale of
articles, or for the exercise of any calling or for the
setting up of any booth or stall and providing for the
levy of fees for such use or occupation; and
(c) regulating the conditions on which permission may
be given by the Kshettra Panchayat under Section 181
for projections over streets and drains and by the Zila
Panchayat under Section 209 for the temporary
occupation of streets.
 D-Markets, slaughter-houses, sale of food, etc.
(a) Prohibiting the use of any place as a slaughter-house, or as a market or shop for the sale of animals
intended for human food or of meat, or of fish, in
default of a licence granted by the Kshettra Panchayat
or otherwise than in accordance with the conditions of
a licence so granted;
(b) prescribing the conditions subject to which and the
circumstances in which, and the areas or localities in
respect of which licences for such use may be granted,
refused, suspended or withdrawn;

6
(c) providing for the inspection of, and regulation of
the conduct of business, in a place used as aforesaid,
so as to secure cleanliness therein or to minimize any
injurious, offensive or dangerous effect arising or
likely to arise therefrom;
(d) providing for the establishment, and for the
regulation and inspection of markets and slaughter-houses, of livery stables, of encamping grounds, of
sarais, of flour-mills, of bakeries, of places for the
manufacture, preparation or sale of specified article of
food or drink, or for keeping or exhibiting animals for
sale or hire or animals of which the produce is sold,
and of places of public entertainment or resort, and for
the proper and cleanly conduct of business therein; and
(e) prescribing the conditions subject to which, and the
circumstances in which, and the areas or locality in
respect of which, licences for the purposes of sub-head
(d) may be granted, refused, suspended or withdrawn,
and fixing the fees payable for such licences, and
prohibiting the establishment of business places,
mentioned in sub-head (d) in default of licence granted
by the Kshettra Panchayat or otherwise than in
accordance with the conditions of a licence so granted.
 E-Offensive trades
(a) Except where and so far as is inconsistent with
anything contained in the Petroleum Act, 1934 (Act
XXX of 1934), or in rules made thereunder,
prohibiting the use of any place, in default of a licence
granted by the Zila Panchayat or otherwise than in
accordance with the conditions of licence so granted,
as a factory or other places of business-
(i) for boiling and storing offal, blood, bones,
guts or rags;
(ii) for the manufacture of leather or leather
goods;
(iii) for melting tallow or sulphur;
(iv) for burning or baking bricks, tiles, pottery
or lime;
(v) for soap-making;
(vi) for oil-boiling;
(vii) for storing hay, straw, thatching grass,
wood, coal or other dangerously inflammable
material;
(viii) for storing petroleum or any inflammable
oil or spirit;
(ix) for storing and pressing cotton and cotton
refuse;

7
(x) for any other purpose if such use is likely to
cause a pubic nuisance or involve risk of fire;
(b) prescribing (but not so as to derogate from any
power conferred on a Zila Panchayat by Section 202),
the circumstances in which and the areas or localities
in respect of which licences may be granted, refused,
suspended or withdrawn; and
(c) providing for the inspection and regulation of the
conduct of business in a place used as aforesaid, so as
to secure cleanliness therein or to minimize any
injurious, offensive, or dangerous effect arising or
likely to arise therefrom."

6. The argument of the appellant would appear to be that
the byelaws impugned are ultra vires the powers. According to the
appellant, while byelaws can be made for issuance of licence, it
cannot require a person to get registered. The impugned byelaws
No. 18 & 19, as translated, read as under:
"18. It will be necessary for the owners of the bazaar
held on individual land to get their bazaar nakhasa
registered with Zila Panchayat within one month from
the date of enforcement of these bye-laws and follow
the standards prescribed in Section 13 and 14 of these
bye-laws. In the event of finding guilty after giving an
adequate opportunity of hearing to such owner, Zila
Panchayat shall be entitled to realize the Tehbazaari
and regulate and manage such bazaars.
19. It shall be necessary for the Gram Panchayat and
private land owners to get their tehbazaari/hat
bazaar/animal bazaar registered with Zila Panchayat.
Following registration fee shall be payable:
 1. For Hat bazaar by Gram Panchayat Rs. 5000.00 per year
 2. For Hat bazaar by Gram Panchayat Rs. 5000.00 per year
 3. For Hat bazaar once in a week Rs.10000.00 per year
 4. For Hat bazaar twice or more in a week Rs.20000.00 per year
 5. For Animal bazaar by once in a week Rs.10000.00 per year
 6. For Animal bazaar twice or more in a week Rs.20000.00 per year"
7. The primary complaint would appear to be that there is
no power to prescribe for byelaws by merely providing for
requirement of registration without anything more. We are of the
view that the use of the word 'regulation' in (b) under B, which

8
provides for establishment and for regulation and inspection of
market place is wide enough to provide for the registration of the
markets. The Zila Panchayat, which would take in fairly large
areas, has a right to provide by byelaws and regulate the markets.
There is no case that Clause 'B' does not apply as such to the extent
of requiring registration.
8. The very idea of registering the market with the
authority is key to regulating the market. It cannot be said that by
insisting for registration, the Zila Panchayat has acted ultra vires its
powers under Section 239. Coming to know of the holding of the
market is the first step in regulating the market with the power in
the nook and corner of the Zila Panchayat. We are certainly of the
view that it would form part of the regulation, requiring the
registration to be done in terms of the byelaws and requiring the
registration under the byelaws cannot in any way be said to be ultra
vires. It is apart from the fact that there is all embraced power as
already referred under Section 239(1) also. In such circumstances,
even on merits, the appellant has not made out any case for
interference with the judgment of the learned Single Judge. The
further prayers sought for the appellant must necessarily fail.
Consequently, the prayers as claimed in the writ petition cannot be
granted and the Appeal fails and the same is dismissed.
9. At this juncture, the learned counsel for the appellant
also has a case that the appellant has, in fact, applied for renewal of
the licence. The dismissal of this Appeal will not stand in the way
of the appellant pursuing his remedy in respect of the Application
which, according to him, he has filed for renewal.
